content:
For a 3-digit number \(N=100a+10b+c\),

\[
\frac{N}{a+b+c}
=10+\frac{9(10a-c)}{a+b+c}.
\]

If \(a\ge 2\), this is already \(>10.5\), so the minimum occurs with \(a=1\). Then

\[
\frac{100+10b+c}{1+b+c}
=10+\frac{9(10-c)}{1+b+c}.
\]

For fixed \(c\), this is minimized by taking the largest possible \(b\). The smallest value occurs at \(c=9,\ b=8\), giving

\[
L=\frac{189}{1+8+9}=\frac{189}{18}=10.5.
\]

Thus

\[
\lfloor 10L\rfloor=\lfloor 105\rfloor=105.
\]

\[
\boxed{105}
\]
